findings.text: The first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is and what makes it different. Someone landing on the Athena site can say what it is before they scroll.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The header explains why the page exists and why it matters: it shows Athena's sourced explanations at work. It also says plainly that the rest of the page is about another project, firstmate, so a newcomer is not confused about the subject.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The next step is linked from the top. A newcomer does not have to read the whole long study to find out what to do.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" linking to #next-steps

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout. It lists no prerequisites, such as Rust, model access or API keys, so a newcomer may get stuck between the repo link and ./setup.sh.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: "Start here" uses terms that its "Words used first" list does not define, including place, capacity, exit 75, spawn and PR. A newcomer has to jump to the Glossary at the end to follow the opening walkthrough.
findings.source: Start here > One piece of work: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: The Counters section refers to transition ids before the Transitions section introduces them. On a first read these ids mean nothing.
findings.source: Counters: "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: Most of the page is dense reference material about firstmate's internals. It is useful for checking the study, but a newcomer who came to learn about Athena will find little more about Athena itself beyond the header and Next steps.
findings.source: Transitions and Claims and sources (cards t1–t11, claims c1–c44)

findings.text: The page is upfront that nothing was run, which helps the reader judge how far to trust the study.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
